# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 15 CHRISTMAS AT SEVEN GULLS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Initially, Hugh and Nell discussed traveling back to Brierley for Christmas, yet in the end, remaining in Seven Gulls was their choice. “It is my wish that the initial Christmas we share as a married couple takes place within our personal dwelling,” Nell declared.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0000 }

Thus it happened that Thirza, accompanied by Mrs. Agatha Sowerby and the twins, arrived at Seven Gulls to spend Christmas. The countenance Thirza possessed resembled that of a female who had sailed all the way around the world. Never previously had she traveled as far as sixty miles from her home; furthermore, she had never partaken of Christmas dinner at any location other than Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0001 }

A huge plum pudding had been baked by Mrs. Agatha and brought along by her. Mrs. Agatha could not be persuaded by anything that a Christmas plum pudding could be made correctly by a college graduate of the younger generation; nevertheless, the house of Nell received her praise.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0002 }

“Nell manages a home well,” she remarked to Thirza inside the guest bedroom on the evening they reached the house. “My inspection covered both her bread box and her garbage bucket. My assessment of a housekeeper relies on those two things every time, that is my method. The pail holds nothing except proper waste, while the bread box lacks any dry crusts. Naturally, your guidance shaped her early on—yet her education continued at college later. The presence of my tobacco stripe quilt on this bed caught my attention, alongside your large circular braided rug placed in front of her parlor fireplace. Those touches make me feel completely comfortable.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0003 }

Nell experienced all the joy she could have hoped for during her initial Christmas in her personal home. Brightness and fine weather marked the day; Christmas Eve had brought the initial thin layer of snow, bestowing beauty upon the world, while the open harbor continued to sparkle.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0004 }

Dinner was attended by Captain Saul and Miss Winifred. Though Lorna and Rufus received an invitation, Lorna declined, stating that they invariably spent Christmas at her Uncle Isaac West’s.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0005 }

“She prefers it that way,” Miss Winifred said to Nell. “Bringing Rufus around unfamiliar people is something she cannot endure. For Lorna, Christmas is consistently a difficult period. Her father and she were accustomed to celebrating it greatly.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0006 }

Miss Winifred and Mrs. Agatha failed to form a particularly strong liking for one another. “Two suns hold not their courses in one sphere.” Yet no conflict arose between them, because Mrs. Agatha remained in the kitchen aiding Nell and Thirza as they prepared dinner, leaving Hugh responsible for entertaining Captain Saul and Miss Winifred—or, more accurately, leaving him to be entertained by the pair, since a conversation between two such longtime companions and rivals was certainly never uninteresting.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0007 }

“It’s been a long time since this place hosted a Christmas dinner, Mistress Carrow,” Captain Saul remarked. “Miss Russell consistently visited her town friends when Christmas came. However, I attended the initial Christmas dinner that this house ever saw—and it was prepared by the schoolmaster’s bride. Sixty years ago today that took place, Mistress Carrow—on a day quite similar to this one—with merely sufficient snow for whitening the hills, while the harbor matched June in its blueness. Being just a boy, I had never received a dinner invitation previously, and my shyness kept me from eating a full portion. I’ve completely recovered from THAT.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0008 }

“The majority of men do,” replied Miss Winifred, stitching with great intensity. Miss Winifred refused to allow her hands to be inactive, even though it was Christmas.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0009 }

Infants arrive with no regard for festive occasions, and an impending birth was anticipated in a destitute home at Glen St. Agnes. Miss Winifred had dispatched a generous meal to that dwelling for its numerous children, intending thereby to consume her own feast with a peaceful mind.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0010 }

“Well, you know, through his stomach is the way to a man’s heart, Winifred,” Captain Saul explained.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0011 }

“I believe you—when he HAS a heart,” Miss Winifred retorted. “I suppose that’s the reason so many women kill themselves cooking—just like poor Amelia Baxter did. She passed away last Christmas morning, and she remarked that it was the first Christmas since she got married that she didn’t have to cook a huge, twenty-plate dinner. It must have been a truly pleasant change for her. Well, she’s been dead for a year, so you’ll soon hear about Horace Baxter taking notice.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0012 }

“I was told he was already paying attention,” Captain Saul remarked, giving Hugh a wink. “Did he not visit your home on a recent Sunday, dressed in his dark funeral suit and wearing a starched collar?”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0013 }

“No, he was not. And he does not need to come either. I might have had him a long time back when he was fresh. I do not desire any second-hand goods, believe ME. Regarding Horace Baxter, he was facing financial troubles a year ago last summer, and he asked the Lord for aid; and when his wife passed away and he received her life insurance he stated he believed it answered his prayer. Was that not just like a man?”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0014 }

“Is there actual evidence that those were his words, Winifred?”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0015 }

“I have the word of the Methodist minister on it—if THAT constitutes proof. Robert Baxter also recounted the identical story to me, though I concede THAT does not amount to evidence. Telling the truth is not something Robert Baxter is frequently known to do.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0016 }

“Now, now, Winifred, I believe he usually speaks truthfully, yet his views shift with such frequency that it occasionally appears as though he were lying.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0017 }

“Believe ME, it frequently seems that way. However, you can rely on one male to justify another. Robert Baxter is someone I cannot tolerate. Simply because 'Behold the bridegroom cometh’ was being performed by the Presbyterian choir as an offering selection when he and Margaret proceeded down the aisle the Sabbath following their wedding, he converted to a Methodist. Arriving tardy meant he got what he deserved! He consistently maintained that the choir deliberately performed it to offend him, as though his significance was that great. Nevertheless, that household constantly viewed themselves as far more crucial than they actually were. Eliphalet, his brother, fancied that Satan was perpetually beside him—yet I was never convinced Satan expended that degree of effort on him.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0018 }

“I—don’t—know,” Captain Saul remarked reflectively. “Eliphalet Baxter’s existence was overly solitary—he did not possess so much as a cat or dog for humanizing companionship. If a person stays isolated, he is extremely prone to associate with the devil—unless God is his companion. I suppose he must select the company he wishes to maintain. Should the devil have constantly remained at Life Baxter’s side, it was undoubtedly because Life preferred his presence.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0019 }

“Resembling a man,” Miss Winifred uttered, then became quiet once more while working on an intricate set of tucks, before Captain Saul intentionally provoked her anew by casually observing:
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0020 }

“I went up to the Methodist church on the previous Sunday morning.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0021 }

“It would have been better if you had stayed home and read your Bible,” Miss Winifred retorted.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0022 }

“Now then, Winifred, I see no injury in attending the Methodist church if there is no sermon at yours. For seventy-six years I have been a Presbyterian, so my theology is hardly going to weigh anchor at this advanced stage.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0023 }

“A poor precedent is being established by this,” Miss Winifred remarked with severity.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0024 }

“Furthermore,” evil Captain Saul kept on, “I desired to listen to some fine singing. A fine choir belongs to the Methodists; and it cannot be denied by you, Winifred, that terrible singing has plagued our church ever since the choir experienced the split.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0025 }

“Supposing the vocal performance is lacking? Their efforts are sincere, and the Almighty perceives no distinction between the call of a crow and the song of a nightingale.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0026 }

“Now, now, Winifred,” Captain Saul uttered gently, “my faith in the Lord’s musical judgment is higher than THAT.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0027 }

“What brought about the disturbance in our choir?” inquired Hugh, who was struggling to contain his laughter.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0028 }

“It originated with the new church, three years back,” Captain Saul replied. “We experienced a terrible period regarding that church's construction—disagreed about the matter of a new location. A mere two hundred yards separated the two locations, yet you would imagine a thousand lay between them given how bitter the dispute became. We were divided into three groups—a first desired the east location, a second preferred the south, and a third stuck to the former one. The battle occurred in bed and at board, and in church and at market. Every old scandal from three generations was pulled from its grave and exposed. It caused three engagements to be broken off. And those meetings held to attempt a resolution! Winifred, will you ever recall the one where old Luther Burns stood and gave an address? HE stated his opinions forcibly.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0029 }

“Be frank, Captain. You are saying he flew into a rage and blasted every single one of them. And they had it coming—they were totally incompetent. Yet what else could come from a group of men? Twenty-seven sessions were conducted by that building committee, and as the twenty-seventh concluded, their progress toward a church was no further along than at the start—actually, it was less, because during a sudden push to speed up the process, they had proceeded to knock the previous church down, leaving us stranded without any church and forced to hold services in the hall.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0030 }

“The Methodists offered us their church, Winifred.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0031 }

“Had us women not simply stepped up and taken control,” Miss Winifred continued, paying no mind to Captain Saul, “the church at Glen St. Agnes still would not be constructed. We declared that WE intended to possess a church, even if the men intended to dispute until the end of time, and that we had grown weary of serving as a source of amusement for the Methodists. Following a SINGLE meeting, we chose a committee and solicited pledges. And we secured them. Whenever any man attempted to give us backtalk, we reminded him that they had attempted to construct a church for two years, meaning our turn had arrived. You can take MY word for it that we silenced them completely, and our church stood completed in six months. Naturally, once it became clear to the men that our resolve was firm, they ceased their arguing and began working, in typical male fashion, the moment they realized they must either do so or forfeit their leadership. Indeed, women are forbidden from preaching or serving as elders; nevertheless, they are capable of constructing churches and raising the funds required for them.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0032 }

“Women are permitted to preach among the Methodists,” Captain Saul said.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0033 }

The look Miss Winifred directed at him was a glare.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0034 }

“I did not state that the Methodists lacked common sense, Captain. My point is, I question whether they possess a great deal of religion.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0035 }

“I take it that you support female suffrage, Miss Winifred,” Hugh remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0036 }

“Believe ME, I’m not eager for the right to vote,” Miss Winifred stated with contempt. “I understand the reality of tidying up the mess men leave behind. However, one of these days, as soon as the men recognize they have plunged the world into a predicament beyond their power to fix, they will happily grant us the vote and shift their burdens onto our shoulders. That is THEIR plan. Oh, it is a blessing that women possess patience, believe ME!”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0037 }

“How about Job?” Captain Saul proposed.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0038 }

“Job! Discovering a patient person was so unusual that when a real one was found, people made sure he would be remembered,” Miss Winifred countered in triumph. “Either way, that quality is not attached to the name. Old Job Taylor across the harbor was the most impatient man ever brought into the world.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0039 }

“Well, as you are aware, he endured a great deal of hardship, Winifred. Her own behavior is indefensible, even by you. The remark made about her by old William MacAllister during her burial remains fresh in my mind, 'There’s nae doot she was a Chreestian wumman, but she had the de’il’s own temper.’”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0040 }

“I guess she WAS making an effort,” Miss Winifred conceded with hesitation, “however, that was no excuse for Job’s remark upon her death. The day she was buried, he traveled back from the cemetery alongside my father. He kept entirely silent until they approached home. At that point, he let out a deep sigh and stated, 'You may not believe it, Stephen, but this is the happiest day of my life!’ Is that not typical of a man?”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0041 }

“I guess the late Mrs. Job rendered his existence rather difficult,” Captain Saul pondered.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0042 }

“Well, decency exists, doesn't it? Though a man may be secretly glad that his wife has died, he doesn't have to announce it to the entire world. And regardless of whether it was a happy day, Job Taylor remarried quickly, as you may have observed. His second spouse knew how to handle him. She certainly made him toe the line! Her initial action was forcing him to bestir himself and erect a gravestone for the original Mrs. Job—and she ensured space remained on it for her name too. She remarked that no one would compel Job to erect a marker for HER.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0043 }

“Apropos of Taylors, doctor, what is the word on Mrs. Penrose Taylor over at the Glen?” inquired Captain Saul.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0044 }

“Although she must labor excessively, her condition is gradually improving,” Hugh answered.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0045 }

“Her spouse also puts in long hours—breeding champion swine,” Miss Winifred remarked. “His exquisite pigs have made him famous. The pride he takes in his pigs far surpasses the pride he feels for his offspring. However, it must be admitted that his pigs achieve absolute perfection, whereas his offspring are fairly useless. The mother he chose for them was a bad choice, and he deprived her of nourishment during her pregnancies and their upbringing. The richest cream was given to his pigs, while his offspring were left with the watery milk.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0046 }

“Winifred, although it causes me pain, there are occasions where I must concur with you,” Captain Saul stated. “You have described Penrose Taylor’s nature precisely. Whenever I look at his unfortunate, pitied children, denied every single thing a child deserves, it poisons my own food and drink for many days following.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0047 }

Answering Nell’s gesture, Hugh walked into the kitchen. After closing the door, Nell delivered a marital reprimand to him.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0048 }

“Hugh, Miss Winifred must no longer be baited by you and Captain Saul. Oh, you have been heard by me—and it simply will not be permitted by me.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0049 }

‘Nell, Miss Winifred is having a wonderful time. You are aware that she is.’
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0050 }

“Oh, it does not matter. The pair of you do not have to encourage her in that manner. The meal can be served now, and, Hugh, do NOT permit Mrs. Agatha to cut up the geese. I am aware that she intends to volunteer for the task since she doubts your ability to perform it correctly. Prove to her that you are capable.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0051 }

“It is something I should manage, given that I have spent the last month examining A-B-C-D carving diagrams,” Hugh stated. “Just refrain from speaking to me during the process, Nell, because should those letters be forced from my mind, my situation will be even more difficult than yours used to be in those past geometry lessons whenever the instructor altered them.”
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0052 }

The geese were carved beautifully by Hugh, a fact even Mrs. Agatha was forced to acknowledge. Everybody partook of them with great pleasure. Radiant with housewifely pride, Nell saw her initial Christmas dinner turn out to be a resounding success. The banquet was both joyful and lengthy, and upon its conclusion, they assembled near the warmth of the red hearth flame, where Captain Saul recounted stories to them until the red sun dipped low above Seven Gulls Harbor, and the Lombardies cast their long blue shadows over the lane's snow.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0053 }

“I need to be returning to the lighthouse,” he eventually stated. “I will barely have sufficient time to travel back on foot prior to sunset. I appreciate the lovely Christmas, Mistress Carrow. Have Master Robin come down to the lighthouse one evening before his departure for home.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0054 }

“Those stone gods are what I want to see,” Robin said eagerly.
{: #nw-v04-c15-p0055 }
